candidate.claim: On matched iso-corpus/iso-tokenizer/iso-token-budget ladders of frozen >=1.3B bases, the content-dependent part of a softmax transformer's in-context update (label-dependent in-context gain on held-out task families the training loss never sees) can be distilled into an explicit rank-8 fast-weight write rule at a canonical 64-d interface that beats a dense-preconditioned-GD superset rule at the same learned interface and compute, and that, frozen and attached strictly after recurrent sublayers through label-free maps, reproduces a measurable fraction of pure-recurrent bases' native content-dependent in-context gain with no demonstrations in the window; a within-hybrid site-type factor and same-family ports separate 'ports across operators' from 'works where softmax exists', and a held-out-language write-A/read-B probe measures whether the writes carry content beyond the frozen encoder's own language invariance.
candidate.mechanism: Frozen source transformer T; episode = 8 formatted demonstrations c_i=(x_i,y_i) plus held-out probes q in Q_i. Two structurally separated passes: Pass W encodes each demonstration alone through the frozen base, pools residuals at K=4 sites (depth 0.25..1.0; on non-transformer bases always the residual after a recurrent sublayer), forms canonical key k_i = P_b^k hbar^k(x_i), value v_i = P_b^k hbar^k(y_i), error e_i = v_i - M_i^k k_i, and the shared rule R_theta (2-layer MLP, ~1e5 params) emits (rho_i in [0,1], eta_i>=0, u_i, w_i in R^64) with M_{i+1}^k = Pi_8[rho_i M_i^k + eta_i u_i w_i^T]; Pass R processes probes with M_i frozen via h^k <- h^k + Q_b^k M_i^k P_b^k h^k. Probes never enter the write stream, so causality is structural, verified by a two-forward-pass prefix-invariance CI gate (no soft L_cause). Interface: M^k in R^{64x64} rank-8; P_b^k (64 x d_b) and Q_b^k (d_b x 64) rank-8, the only base-specific parameters. Derived superset at the same interface, R_GD: u_i = W e_i, w_i = k_i, eta_i = eta_0 (i+1)^{-gamma}/(||k_i||^2+eps)^beta, rho_i = rho_0 with learned W in R^{64x64} and four scalars, containing delta, Kaczmarz, OSDN-diagonal and Falcon-normalised rules as special cases, trained with the same loss, P/Q co-fitting and compute. Distillation on the source, distillation families only: L_dist = sum_i sum_q KL(p_T(.|q,c_{<=i}) || p_{T,M_i}(.|q)) with truncated BPTT through 8 writes over theta (or W and scalars), P_T, Q_T. Stage-D equivariance: L_eq = ||Delta M(c_i) - Delta M(c_i^B)||_F^2 on human-translated parallel demonstrations for training language pairs en-{de,es,zh} only; evaluation is behavioural write-en/read-B on held-out languages. Port: freeze the rule; fit P_b' by ridge regression of span-pooled target residuals onto the source's canonical keys and Q_b' by functional matching of next-token log-prob shifts under a fixed bank of injected random rank-1 M's, both on 2k x 512-token FineWeb-Edu sequences with no task family; every rule (R_theta, R_GD, random-theta) gets its own distillation and its own port by the identical procedure. Logged per write: effective step s_i = eta_i||u_i|| ||w_i||, rho_i, hash-chained write log, reset attestation.
candidate.what_is_new: Downgraded to a recombination: each component has a prior (context->per-model weight updates: Generative Adapter, Doc-to-LoRA, Can GD Simulate Prompting; analytic ICL-as-low-rank-patch; frozen-LM state transfer: Cache-to-Cache, XKV, KV translation; learned/derived fast-weight rules within one family: TTT, Modular TTT, Falcon, Fast Weight Layers, SRWM; cross-architecture weight distillation). The delta is the transferred OBJECT — the write rule (HOW) distilled from one transformer's in-context behaviour, frozen, and attached to bases of other operator families that have no KV cache to receive state — plus two tests with no located precedent: a head-to-head against a preconditioned-GD superset at the same learned interface, and a write-A/read-B held-out-language probe. No direct prior art found through 2026-09-01 under the coverage in the note's section 11 (6 hostsearch calls this wave plus the wave-1 refuter's 31 queries; Semantic Scholar and OpenReview bodies unavailable). Pre-registered collapse: if R_theta ties a label-trained sibling rule, the result is reported as an instance of Fast Weight Layers / SRWM.

The repaired pilot still cannot attribute its endpoints to "the transformer's content-dependent in-context update, distilled and ported"; both pre-registered Stage-B outcomes and the Stage-C architecture reading are explained by matched-control asymmetries or inert counterfactuals.

1) The primary placebo is not matched across the two arms it is meant to compare. r_TL's numerator is acc(gold writes) - acc(shuffled writes). Because each demonstration c_i is encoded as one sequence, v_i = P*hbar(y_i | x_i) is the base's residual at the label token IN THE CONTEXT of the input, and hidden states at that position encode whether the pair is coherent/true (Azaria & Mitchell 2304.13734: 71-83% truth classification from hidden states; Marks & Tegmark 2310.06824: linear truth directions). R_theta is a 1e5-parameter MLP trained only on coherent gold episodes ("random-label episodes appear nowhere in any training objective"), so shuffled writes are off-manifold inputs whose write behaviour (degenerate, suppressed or amplified) is unconstrained; R_GD is linear in e_i = v_i - M k_i, so the same perturbation moves its M smoothly and its shuffled M keeps the permutation-invariant label-space (TR) component. Hence acc(shuffled) can collapse toward zero-shot for R_theta while staying at TR level for R_GD, inflating r_TL(R_theta) - r_TL(R_GD) with zero content (pairing) information. The native denominator G_TL keeps TR in the reference (Function Vectors Table 2: GPT-J still scores 39.1% on shuffled-label prompts; Pan et al. 2305.09731; Min et al. 2202.12837), so the ratio is not "content-dependent gain reproduced" for R_theta. No TR-fidelity gate (rule's shuffled-write gain must match the teacher's random-label gain) and no in-distribution random-label episodes exist in the design, so P1's headline >=0.15 gap is exactly the signature of "nonlinear rule on OOD placebo vs linear rule".

2) The nested comparison cannot identify the object named in the claim. R_theta's function class contains R_GD (u=We, w=k, eta from i and ||k||, constant rho are all representable), so any structure in the teacher map outside GD, including surface biases (majority/recency 2102.09690, order sensitivity 2104.08786) or the coherence gate above, produces a win; nothing in the pilot measures fidelity to T on held-out families (error agreement with T, per-step i accuracy curve, order sensitivity), only accuracy ratios that any good associative rule produces. The sibling test is one-sided: a tie collapses to FWL/SRWM (pre-registered), but a distilled-over-label-trained win is the standard soft-target distillation effect (Hinton 1503.02531), not evidence that the HOW is T's.

3) The K1 branch is also unidentified. Eligible families (G_TL >= 10 at 1.3B) will be dominated by exact-recall binding tasks, where the delta/Kaczmarz family IS the associative-recall solution (2406.06484; 2402.01032), and a rank-8 M is at capacity for 8 pairs; Dherin et al. 2507.16003 already show a with-context pass is mathematically equivalent to a minimal low-rank patch. An R_GD tie therefore reflects the task/interface, and the announced negative result ("first behavioural confirmation that T's content-dependent update is preconditioned GD") does not follow.

4) The architecture-causal reading rests on an inert counterfactual. startlux config.json puts attention at 0-based layers 2,5,...,23, so site set G (after 4/10/16/22) and set A (after 5/11/17/23) are adjacent layers on one shared residual stream with softmax attention downstream in both; the injection is consumed by downstream layers, not by the preceding sublayer, so ">= 0.7x" passes trivially and the "<= 0.5x -> works only where softmax exists" branch cannot fire. The rule is operator-agnostic by construction (it acts in the canonical 64-d space; the operator enters only through frozen features and the re-fitted P/Q), so Stage C measures cross-architecture linear alignability of residuals (expected: Platonic Representation Hypothesis 2405.07987; Cache-to-Cache 2510.03215), an n=1-per-checkpoint retrofit result read as an architecture claim. K3 conflates "ported R_theta <= ported R_GD" (both port equally) with "the rule does not port".

5) Counterfactual references are inconsistent on targets: the eligibility gate is applied to the source T only, so r_TL(b') on a recurrent target with weak native G_TL is inflated exactly where there is least to reproduce, making P2's ">= 4 of 6 targets >= 0.40" easiest on the weakest targets. Stage D's gap shrinkage is attributable to the co-fitted P learning to project out a shared language subspace (R_GD with lambda_eq > 0 is not run, 6 D1 runs), not to the rule.

Net: as written, neither Stage-B outcome distinguishes the mechanism from its strongest control (a learned/derived associative rule at the same interface), and the port's architecture claim has no live counterfactual. Fixes exist (train both rules on random-label episodes and gate on TR fidelity; add teacher-fidelity endpoints on H; gate G_TL per base; drop the site-type factor; run R_GD with lambda_eq) but they are not in the pilot.

disc.delta_one_sentence: Both distill the frozen model's prompted predictions into a per-example update via KL, but the prior meta-learns an initialization of the LM's own weights (full or rank-1 LoRA) so that one plain fixed-LR gradient step on the new text emulates prompting, whereas Text A keeps the base frozen and learns the update operator itself — a tiny MLP write rule (decay plus rank-1 step, no test-time gradients) into an external rank-8 fast-weight memory behind fixed low-rank P/Q ports, with structural write/read separation, a GD-family rule as an in-interface baseline, translation-equivariance training, and cross-base porting by refitting only P/Q — none of which the prior addresses.

judges.fatal_defect: The primary endpoint r_TL = (gold-write gain minus shuffled-label-write gain) is not a matched placebo across the two arms it compares: R_theta is a nonlinear 1e5-parameter MLP trained only on coherent gold episodes, so shuffled-label demonstrations (whose label-token residuals encode incoherence, per linear truth-direction results) are off-manifold inputs with unconstrained write behaviour, while R_GD is linear in e_i and degrades smoothly, retaining the task-recognition component. The pre-registered P1 headline (r_TL gap >= 0.15) is therefore exactly the signature of 'nonlinear rule on OOD placebo vs linear rule' and can be produced with zero content/pairing information; no TR-fidelity gate or teacher-fidelity endpoint exists to catch it, so neither Stage-B branch (win or K1 tie) identifies 'the transformer's content-dependent in-context update'. Compounding this, the claim_scope 'architecture-causal' is a retrofit on pretrained checkpoints with no matched from-scratch arm (hard rule 8), and the startlux site-type counterfactual (after-layer-4 vs after-layer-5 on one shared residual stream with softmax attention downstream of both) is inert, so the '<= 0.5x' K3 branch cannot fire.
judges.highest_impact_fix: Make the placebo symmetric and add teacher fidelity as the primary endpoint: (1) include the teacher's own shuffled-label episodes in the distillation set for every rule (R_theta, R_GD, label-trained sibling, random-theta) so the KL target on random-label writes is p_T under random labels, and add a CI gate on every arm requiring the rule's shuffled-write gain to match the teacher's random-label gain within a stated tolerance (TR-fidelity gate) before any r_TL is reported; (2) add held-out-family teacher-fidelity endpoints (per-query error agreement with T, per-step i accuracy curve, order-sensitivity match) alongside r_TL, so a rule that beats R_GD on accuracy but not on fidelity is reported as 'a better associative rule', not 'T's update'; (3) apply the G_TL >= 10 eligibility gate per base, not only on the source; (4) relabel claim_scope to portability-protocol / attachment-capability (or add an iso-parameter from-scratch matched arm) and replace the startlux adjacent-layer site factor with a causal ablation that removes downstream attention from the read path; (5) cite and discriminate against Jeong 2603.22329/2603.16413, FAAST 2605.04651, 2605.26099 and 2406.02847 to lift the novelty-coverage cap. These changes fit inside the existing Stage-B ledger (they reuse the same episodes and forward passes).

candidate.claim: In gated delta-rule/SSM layers (GDN, KDA) forgetting and write gates tick once per token, so equal content costs a high-fertility language proportionally more cumulative forgetting and write mass. Three ordered claims: (C1) released GDN/KDA gates do not self-normalize this (cumulative log-decay over a translated sentence scales with its token count); (C2) rescaling per-token log-decay for language L by 1/r on a frozen base hybrid moves translation-paired recall with an optimum near r = fertility(L), fertility-specifically (Thai/Chinese, non-Latin but low-fertility on this tokenizer, behave like English); (C3) a scale-invariant, anchored span-parity auxiliary loss on the existing gate statistics, supervised by sentence-aligned parallel text at training time only, closes the recall gap at unchanged per-language BPB with no inference change - pre-registered for EQUIVALENCE against a per-language constant gate rescale, since the measured within-language span-ratio CV (0.17-0.24) bounds what span-level supervision can add.
candidate.mechanism: GDN (transformers qwen3_5 / fla gated_deltanet): S_t = alpha_t S_{t-1}(I - beta_t k_t k_t^T) + beta_t v_t k_t^T, g_t = log alpha_t = -exp(A_log) softplus(a_t + dt_bias), beta_t = sigmoid(b_t). For an aligned span s: forgetting mass F(s) = -sum_{t in s} g_t, write mass W(s) = sum_{t in s} beta_t; under a per-token clock F(s_L)/F(s_en) ~ fertility ratio. Tallec & Ollivier (1804.11188) prove gates give quasi-invariance to time warps, so 'LM loss already learned the warp' (R_F ~ 1) is the null phase 0 tests first. Phase-0 training-free interventions via hooks on the 24 GDN layers of Qwen3.5-4B-Base: constant decay surgery g'_t = g_t / r on a log2 grid incl. r = f_L; span-oracle surgery g'_t = g_t / r_s with r_s = |s_L|/|s_en| per aligned NTREX sentence; write surgery beta'_t = 1-(1-beta_t)^{1/r} (compounded write over r tokens equals one baseline token's; coupling with the erase term reported as a caveat). Phase-1 treatment (arm b), on parallel-view batches with each translation processed monolingually and coupled only through span sums: L = L_LM + lambda sum_{(s_a,s_b)} sum_{layers,heads} (log(F(s_a)+eps) - log(F(s_b)+eps))^2 + lambda_W (same for W) + kappa (mean_{t in en} g_t - anchor_en)^2, where the log-ratio form is exactly invariant to a global rescale of g (removes the wave-1 'forget less' shortcut) and anchor_en is the detached EMA of the model's own English per-token mean log-decay at end of warm-up (pins the English forgetting budget). Only gate parameters receive the auxiliary gradient; the loss is causal by construction and vanishes at inference. The wave-1 shared content clock c_t is demoted to an optional confirmation parameterization (a Mamba-Delta x GDN recombination).
candidate.what_is_new: A recombination, not a new gate: (a) a per-language cumulative forgetting/write ledger on released GDN/KDA checkpoints; (b) a fertility-predicted clock-surgery dose-response as a training-free causal test of 'the state clock ticks per token'; (c) a translation-paired recall probe with script-neutral 4-digit answers and n-way matched-content distractors (the seq-operators G1 / benchmarks-eval G2 instrument); (d) cross-lingually supervised gate statistics (scale-invariant span-parity loss) pre-registered against a per-language constant. Vs Gated DeltaNet/KDA: gates trained by LM loss with no per-language analysis. Vs Tallec & Ollivier 2018: time-warp invariance proved but never measured or supervised across languages. Vs Mamba: Delta_t is a per-token clock whose totals are never supervised across translations (arm (ii) acknowledged as a recombination and demoted). Vs MAGNET/H-Net/Parity-aware BPE: parity at segmentation/tokenizer level; here the tokenizer is fixed and parity lives inside the operator with inference unchanged. No direct prior art found through 2026-09-01 under the coverage in the note's section 11 (abstract-level; DDG/Semantic Scholar/WebSearch unavailable).

Coverage: 32 hostsearch calls (arXiv API route 429-blocked on 20/22 queries; HF Papers, OpenReview, Crossref succeeded), 6 WebSearch sweeps, 15 WebFetch abstract checks, grep of 15 pre-pulled arXiv feeds, ft X-bookmarks, gh. Nearest partial prior is Hirschi 2604.02474 (Apr 2026), which rescales LSTM time constants by a known time-warp factor for transfer across physical timescales -- the same operation as the candidate's constant decay surgery g'=g/r but on LSTMs for dynamical systems, with no language/tokenization/fertility framing, no recall probe and no auxiliary loss; it must be cited as a mechanism ancestor alongside Tallec & Ollivier 1804.11188 (theory only, never measured across languages). Hossain et al. IJCNLP 2025 / 2512.15653 characterize what Mamba forgets (rare tokens, math, entities, non-standard dialects) observationally, without per-language or gate-level analysis. GDN, KDA, GDN-2, FoX, Adaptive Memory Decay 2605.06946 and Disentangle-to-Decay learn decay by LM loss with no per-language analysis or parallel-data supervision. SSMs-for-MT 2407.05489, MLMA (ASR), LoResMT Indic SSM QA, mLongRR, Stuffed Mamba and tokenizer-tax papers touch multilingual or forgetting but never link fertility to cumulative gate mass. Verdict not-refuted is held at moderate confidence because the arXiv full-text API was unavailable and the C1/C2 ledger+surgery component is a straightforward Tallec-Ollivier/Hirschi recombination; the C3 span-parity loss and the fertility-predicted dose-response test have no located precedent.

Substrate and numbers check out (Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B-Base @1001bb4d: 24 linear_attention + 8 full_attention layers, vocab 248320, mark-aware [\p{L}\p{M}]+ pre-tokenizer; transformers qwen3_5 computes beta=b.sigmoid(), g=-exp(A_log)*softplus(a+dt_bias) in Python so hooks are feasible; the candidate's fertilities and span-ratio CVs reproduce exactly on the real tokenizer over NTREX@468c6b6: tam 2.744, ben 2.164, hin 2.073, ell 2.119, ukr 1.792, hun 1.706, fin 1.627, pol 1.605, kor 1.284, tha 1.174, zho 0.931; CV 0.19-0.23). The identification fails on the mechanism, not the measurement. (1) Strongest control for C3 is conceded and decided by arithmetic: the span-oracle differs from the per-language constant only through per-sentence r_s variation, and the recall endpoint integrates it over d>=8 sentences; measured block-level cumulative-forgetting differences are 5-9% (1 SD) at d=32 and 8-14% at d=8 (fert.py), i.e. ~0.1 in log r against a grid step of 0.35, a second-order (<1 EM point) perturbation at any dose-response optimum. The per-cell TOST (SE 1.3, margin 3) has ~49% power even at a true zero difference, so per-language K5 is a coin flip while pooled K5 fires with certainty; either way phase 0 cannot show the parallel view matters, and phase-1 arm b vs learned-constant arm c inherits the same integrated endpoint. (2) The placebo is not inert: under a per-token clock, within-language log F(s) variance is dominated by sentence-length variance (CV(|s_L|)=0.50-0.53 on NTREX vs cross-language span-ratio CV 0.19-0.23; fert3.py). Minimizing the same-language random-pair log-ratio drives F(s) toward independence from token count, a per-sentence content clock: exactly the token-count-invariant forgetting the treatment installs and the demoted arm (ii). The F-space proof (zero gradient projection on the between-language log-mean) says nothing about parameter space where a_proj/A_log/dt_bias are shared across languages; the pre-registered 'e < 15% of b' either fails under a true mechanism or, if e closes the gap, reproduces K5. (3) C2's fertility-specificity is confounded with resourcedness: log fertility vs log CC-MAIN-2026-34 page share is Pearson -0.85 (Spearman -0.71) across the 8 high-fertility languages and -0.78 across all 11 phase-0 languages (fert2.py), so the P3 slope on log f_L is equally a slope on training exposure. Thai (0.37% CC) only matches the ~0.4% tier (fin 0.38%, hun 0.53%); no low-fertility control exists at the <=0.2% tier where hin/ben/tam sit (Malay f=1.157, 0.086% would be one and is omitted), and on this tokenizer no high-resource language has f>=1.5 (rus 1.423/6.9%, tur 1.429/1.4% are the closest and are omitted), so the language set as written cannot break the correlation; a training-free synthetic-fertility arm is impossible on a frozen model. P4 (English interaction) is bounded by the English ceiling (gain <= 100-EM(en)) and presumes r*(en) is interior at r~1. (4) Counterfactual inconsistency: phase 0 runs on a frozen 3:1 hybrid whose 8 full-attention layers (head_dim 256) can retrieve a 4-digit code at <=4k tokens with no recurrent state, and no attention-path ablation is included, so EM is not a clean readout of GDN forgetting; a flat dose-response or grid-edge optimum (plausible because the probe puts no cost on over-retention and delta-rule erase handles interference) is read as K2 'clock not the bottleneck' and kills the pure-GDN phase 1 for a hybrid-specific reason. (5) Retrofit read as architecture: under the candidate's own expected outcome (P5/K5) the surviving deliverable is an inference-time per-language gate rescale on a released checkpoint plus a ledger, carried under claim_scope 'architecture-causal'. Endpoint != objective holds (recall EM/BPB vs gate-statistic loss), and C1 survives as a measurement. Verdict: the pilot as written cannot distinguish the span-parity mechanism from a per-language constant or from a monolingual per-sentence budget, and cannot distinguish fertility from resourcedness in C2.

disc.delta_one_sentence: GDN (2412.06464) contributes only the substrate — the gated delta recurrence S_t = alpha_t S_{t-1}(I - beta_t k_t k_t^T) + beta_t v_t k_t^T, its chunkwise-parallel WY training algorithm, and SWA/Mamba2 hybrids, with alpha_t and beta_t learned solely through LM loss and no mention of multilingual behavior, tokenization fertility, time-warp invariance, gate auxiliary losses, or gate rescaling — whereas Text A leaves that recurrence untouched and adds a cross-lingual fertility-invariance layer on top of it: training-free per-token log-decay and write-gate surgery scaled by span-length (fertility) ratios, and a gate-parameter-only auxiliary loss on parallel data that equalizes span-summed log-forgetting mass and write mass across aligned translations (global-rescale-invariant log-ratio form, English-anchored via detached EMA), so the prior cannot dominate a mechanism it does not contain; the only overlap is that GDN's data-dependent gating is exactly the null hypothesis (R_F ~ 1 via Tallec-Ollivier quasi-invariance) that Text A's Phase 0 is designed to test first.

judges.fatal_defect: C2, the only causal claim the pilot can actually test, is not identified as written. (1) On the Qwen3.5 tokenizer the eight high-fertility languages have log fertility correlated -0.85 (Pearson; -0.71 Spearman) with log Common Crawl share, and the language set contains no high-fertility/high-resource language (rus 1.42, tur 1.43 omitted) and no low-fertility language in the <=0.2% resource tier where hin/ben/tam sit (Malay f=1.16, 0.086% omitted), so the pre-registered P3 slope of log r*(L) on log f_L is equally a slope on training exposure; Thai/Chinese only control script, not resourcedness. (2) The EM readout runs on a frozen 3:1 hybrid whose 8 full-attention layers (head_dim 256) can retrieve a 4-digit code at <=4k tokens without the recurrent state, and there is no attention-path ablation and no off-ceiling calibration (pure 1.3B GDN scores 92-100 on S-NIAH-2 at 1-4k), so a flat dose-response or grid-edge optimum is indistinguishable from 'probe saturated / bypassed by attention' yet is pre-registered to fire K2 and kill phase 1. Compounding this, the candidate's own arithmetic (block-level span-ratio variation of 5-14%, ~0.1 in log r vs a 0.35 grid step; per-cell TOST power ~49% at a true zero) pre-decides K5, so the surviving deliverable under the expected outcome is an inference-time per-language gate rescale plus a ledger on a released checkpoint, which rule 8 forbids carrying as 'architecture-causal'. Novelty coverage is also incomplete (arXiv API blocked on 20/22 queries, no ACL Anthology/patent/Chinese sweep, no PRISMA counts) and Hirschi 2604.02474 (constant time-warp rescale of LSTM gates, g'=g/r) is an uncited mechanism ancestor; the 74 and 79 caps both apply but are not binding at this total.
judges.highest_impact_fix: Make phase 0 a within-model, GDN-borne, confound-breaking dose-response before spending anything on phase 1. (a) Decorrelate fertility from resourcedness in the language grid: add rus (f 1.42, 6.9% CC), tur (1.43, 1.4%), msa (1.16, 0.09%) and keep mya (4.18) as stress, and pre-register C2 as the fertility coefficient in a two-regressor fit of log r*(L)-log r*(en) on log f_L and log CC share, requiring the fertility coefficient's 95% CI to exclude 0.2 after partialling out resourcedness (report the partial slope, not the marginal one). (b) Make EM a readout of the recurrent state: run every dose-response cell twice, once as written and once with the 8 full-attention layers prevented from attending from the query to distractor/fact positions (key mask on the distractor span, or fact positions only visible through GDN state), and additionally run the same grid on an attention-free multilingual subject (fla-hub/rwkv7-1.5B/2.9B-world) so 'clock irrelevant' and 'bypassed by attention' get different signatures; extend d to {8,32,64,128} (or K to 16/32) to get EM(en) off ceiling, which fits in ~10-12 GPU-h and stays under the 16 GPU-h lite line. (c) Relabel honestly: claim_scope for the phase-0 deliverable is systems-pipeline/portability (ledger + per-language gate normalization recipe), with architecture-causal reserved for phase 1 and gated on the partial-slope test above; cite Hirschi 2604.02474 next to Tallec & Ollivier as the mechanism ancestor of the constant surgery. (d) Replace the same-language placebo e with one that is inert in parameter space (e.g., pairs matched on token count so the loss cannot learn token-count-invariant forgetting), or drop the 'e < 15% of b' criterion and pre-register e as a second mechanism arm.

judges.fatal_defect: The phase-0 causal readout is not a readout of the GDN clock. Every C2 inference (P3 dose-response slope, P4 interaction, K2/K3 kills) is taken from exact-match recall of a 4-digit code at <=4k tokens on Qwen3.5-4B-Base, a 3:1 hybrid whose 8 full-attention layers (head_dim 256) can retrieve the code with no recurrent state, and the pilot includes neither an attention-path ablation nor an off-ceiling calibration (K=8, d<=32; pure 1.3B GDN already scores 92-100 on S-NIAH at 1-4K per the GDN paper, and 2606.15378 shows hybrid long-range retrieval is carried by attention). A flat dose-response or grid-edge optimum therefore cannot be distinguished from 'probe saturated / bypassed by attention', yet it is pre-registered to fire K2 and cancel the pure-GDN phase 1; conversely a positive slope on log f_L is equally a slope on training exposure, since log fertility and CC page share correlate at -0.85 across the eight high-fertility languages and the language set contains no low-fertility language at the <=0.2% resource tier and no high-resource language with f>=1.5. The identification refuter (0.8) and feasibility refuter independently converged on this. Secondary: the same-language placebo e is not inert (sentence-length CV ~0.5 dominates within-language F variance, so minimizing it installs a per-sentence content clock through shared a_proj/A_log/dt_bias), per-cell TOST has ~49% power at true zero, span-oracle vs constant differs by ~0.1 in log r against a 0.35 grid step, and Hirschi 2604.02474 (time-constant rescale by a known warp factor, the exact operation of the constant surgery) is absent from closest_priors. Under the candidate's own expected outcome (P5/K5) the surviving deliverable is an inference-time per-language gate rescale on a released checkpoint, which rule 8 forbids labelling architecture-causal without the gated phase 1.
judges.highest_impact_fix: Make phase 0 a clean clock readout inside the 16 GPU-h envelope (~10-13 GPU-h): (1) add an attention-path control on the same frozen checkpoint - either mask the 8 full-attention layers' keys at the fact positions during the query (attention-blind arm) or, cheaper and cleaner, add an attention-free multilingual subject ladder (fla-hub/rwkv7-{0.4B,1.5B,2.9B}-world, World v3 data, fla/ops/rwkv7 present) and pre-register that C2 kills fire only if they replicate on the attention-free subject; (2) push the probe off ceiling with d in {64,128} and/or K in {16,32} and report the baseline EM(en) curve before any surgery so r*(L) is interior by construction; (3) break the fertility-resourcedness correlation in the language set by adding Malay (f=1.16, 0.09% CC) at the low-fertility/low-resource corner and Russian (f=1.42, 6.9%) and Turkish (f=1.43) at the high-fertility/high-resource corner, then pre-register P3 as a partial slope on log f_L controlling for log CC share; (4) replace the same-language placebo e with a length-stratified placebo (pairs matched on |s| within 5%) so the loss cannot install a content clock; (5) pool the TOST across languages (power >0.8) and state the per-cell test as descriptive; (6) cite Hirschi 2604.02474 as the mechanism ancestor of the constant surgery. With (1)-(3) in place a flat dose-response becomes a genuine K2 and a positive slope becomes fertility-specific evidence; without them phase 0 cannot decide C2 in either direction.

candidate.claim: Learned sparse-attention indexers of the DSA/QSA class, distilled only from full attention, carry an excess cross-lingual selection gap beyond the gap of their own distillation target; supervising the detached indexer with corpus-given sentence alignments from bilingual document pairs (a training view that never touches main attention; inference unchanged) removes most of that excess gap on held-out languages at matched achieved token budget, and the fix appears in generation exact match, not only in selection-recall proxies.
candidate.mechanism: Indexer I_t(s) = sum_j w_{t,j} ReLU(q^I_{t,j} . k^I_s), S_t = Top-k_s I_t(s), sparse layer attends over S_t only (token form as GLM-5.3-Flash DSA: 32x128 heads, top-k 2048, kpool 4; block form as Qwen3.8-Flash-Next QSA: 4 heads x 128, 1 kv head, compress 4, budget 2048 — both read from HF configs 2026-09-01). Distillation L_I = KL(P_t || softmax_s I_t(s)) with P_t a fixed aggregation of the frozen layer's full attention; head-sum (DSA), max-pool (QSA) and retrieval-head-weighted aggregations are separate arms. No gradient reaches the backbone. Translation view: for a document pair (D_a, D_b) with the corpus's own sentence alignment {(u_i, v_i)}, build C = [D_b; <sep>; D_a] and the reverse; for a query token t in sentence u_i define A(t) = tokens of v_i, mapped to indexer granularity N(A(t)); L_x = -(1/|Q|) sum_{t in Q} log sum_{s in N(A(t))} softmax_s(I_t(s)); L_I' = L_I + lambda_x L_x (lambda_x in {0.25, 0.5}). No external word aligner (OmniAlign/CTFAlign removed); the wave-1 L_eq unbalanced-Sinkhorn arm is dropped (no differentiable implementation, not needed). Same-loss-form controls: L_perm (labels permuted within document; negative control) and L_half (log-mass on the whole other-language half; tests whether pushing mass across the language boundary suffices). Evaluation quantities are never computed from alignment labels.
candidate.what_is_new: Downgraded per the wave-1 novelty caveats: the loss is a recognizable transfer of NMT supervised/guided attention (Liu et al. 2016 arXiv 1609.04186; Chen et al. 2016 arXiv 1607.01628; Garg et al. 2019 arXiv 1909.02074), which supervise the main encoder-decoder attention with aligner labels. The delta is (i) the object — a detached top-k selection indexer of a decoder-only sparse-attention LM whose main attention never sees the signal; (ii) the label — corpus-given sentence alignment on concatenated bilingual documents, no aligner; (iii) the instrument — cross-lingual selection recall of an indexer measured against its own distillation target (excess gap xi) on held-out languages at matched achieved budget. Versus DSA (2512.02556): adds an alignment-supervised selection term and per-language selection measurement. Versus QSA (2608.30320): a drop-in indexer objective for its CPT indexer; QSA's KL + max-pool is the baseline arm. Versus SpotAttention (2606.22874, frozen-Qwen3/Qwen3.5 KL selector at English dense parity, non-English untested): its cross-lingual audit plus a fix. The load-bearing new claim is the diagnostic P1, which no source reports. No direct prior art found through 2026-09-01 under the wave-1 novelty search (9 arXiv, 4 HF-papers, 7 WebSearch, DSA and QSA full text) plus today's arXiv API query (abs:indexer AND abs:"sparse attention" AND multilingual/cross-lingual/translation -> MiniMax MSA, FlashMemory-DeepSeek-V4, Dynamic Sparse Attention, none multilingual) and HF-papers query (MGAL 2608.20853 benchmark only).

closest_priors.title: DeepSeek-V3.2 (DeepSeek Sparse Attention, lightning indexer)
closest_priors.delta: Indexer trained by KL to head-summed attention (2.1B-token frozen warm-up, 943.7B tokens unfrozen), no per-language analysis; ours adds an alignment-supervised selection term and measures per-language selection recall against the target.

closest_priors.title: On the Design of Qwen3.8-Next Architecture (QSA)
closest_priors.delta: Compressed-block indexer with max-pooled KL target at continued pretraining, only aggregate MMMLU reported; ours is a drop-in objective for that indexer and uses the QSA recipe as the baseline arm.

closest_priors.title: SpotAttention: Plug-In Block-Sparse Routing for Pretrained Long-Context Transformers
closest_priors.delta: Frozen-Qwen3/Qwen3.5 KL-distilled selector with dual top-p budgets reaches English dense parity to 128K, non-English untested; ours is its cross-lingual audit plus a fix, and its top-p rule is a mandatory control (no public code found; re-implemented).

closest_priors.title: Lost in Compression: A Controlled Cross-Lingual Audit of Extractive Prompt Compressors
closest_priors.delta: Shows the cross-lingual selection gap of learned compressors tracks supervision data, with budgets matched in the target tokenizer; its protocol is adopted, but it studies prompt compressors, not attention indexers.

closest_priors.title: Neural Machine Translation with Supervised Attention (Liu et al.)
closest_priors.delta: Supervises main NMT attention with aligner-derived labels; ours supervises a detached selection indexer in a decoder-only LM with corpus-given sentence alignment, inference unchanged.

closest_priors.title: MGAL: A Multilingual Granularity-Aware Long-Context Benchmark
closest_priors.delta: Multilingual position-aware long-context benchmark on UN reports in 6 languages; an endpoint, with no sparse-attention component.

P2: arm (c) KL + L_x versus arm (b) KL-only on identical bilingual concatenations (the counterfactual for every L_x claim) recovers >= 60% of xi on held-out language pairs never seen by L_x, with monolingual E1 within 1 point of (b) and English RULER-style E3 within 0.5 points; and (c) beats the permuted-label arm (d) and the other-half-mass arm (e) by at least half of the (c)-(b) recovery.

kill_conditions: Phase 0: xi <= 5 points on both bases for both indexer forms — the indexer adds no cross-lingual bottleneck beyond its own target; publish the localization negative and stop.
(c) - (b) recovers < 30% of xi on held-out pairs — bilingual document exposure alone does the work.
(d) L_perm or (e) L_half achieves >= 80% of (c)'s recovery — the loss form or cross-language mass push, not alignment content, is the mechanism.
Any training-free control at matched achieved budget (top-p, larger k at matched latency, PIVOT-style, NSA-pooled, SWA + sinks) recovers >= 80% of (c) - (b).
The dense + alignment-supervised LoRA control recovers >= 80% of the gain — not selection-specific.
E1 (selection) gains without E2 (generation EM) gains, or gains confined to in-training languages.
Any held-out language's E1 recall drops > 2 points versus (b), or monolingual E3 drops > 0.5 points (under- or over-selection of a language).
Phase-0 headroom gate fails on both bases (dense monolingual E2 < 60% at 8K): only E1/xi are reported and the E2 claim is withdrawn, not rescued by a larger model inside this contract.
candidate.cheapest_decisive_pilot: Phase 0 (the pilot of record, <= 4 GPU-h on 8x H100, one Slurm job). CPU doctors first: bilingual-concatenation builder from ParaDocs/TED2020 with sentence-alignment map and L_x mass accounting and permutation-sensitivity checks; NIAH/TR-NIAH builder with per-prompt achieved-token ledger (Qwen tokenizer) and exact-50-gram + MinHash dedup of FineWeb-2 haystacks and training docs against Belebele/WMT24++/FLORES+ with logged counts; synthetic permuted-vocabulary toy as a sanity check. GPU: frozen qwen3-0.6b-base (Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-Base @ da87bfb608c14b7cf20ba1ce41287e8de496c0cd; indexers on all 28 layers) and frozen qwen3.5-4b (Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B @ 851bf6e806efd8d0a36b00ddf55e13ccb7b8cd0a; indexers only on its 8 full-attention layers 3,7,...,31 — production placement); KL-only indexers in token form (4x128, DSA) and block form (4x128, 1 kv head, compress 4, QSA) x 3 seeds = 6 per base, all trained in one shared teacher stream (no gradient into the backbone) on 50M tokens = 6,104 x 8K sequences (half bilingual concatenations, half monolingual FineWeb-2). Eval: E1 needle-token selection recall and the target's own recall R^T on 3,000 sealed Belebele prompts in held-out languages (ja, ko, bn, ta, el, he, ka cross-script; id, tr, sw, nl, it same-script), 3 needle positions, 8K/16K/32K, dense distributions computed only for query rows; dense E2 headroom check on 600 prompts per base. Budget at assumed 30% MFU (297 TFLOPS) and 2.0 TB/s effective, half the ~60% MFU llm.c reports for GPT-2 124M (10B tokens in ~90 min on 8x A100, github.com/karpathy/llm.c/discussions/481): teacher 0.6B 1.4e17 FLOP = 0.13 h; attention-probability materialization 7.3e14 B = 0.10 h; teacher 4B hybrid 4.0e17 FLOP = 0.37 h + 0.03 h; 12 indexers fwd+bwd + score traffic 0.25 h; E1 eval ~9e17 FLOP = 0.85 h; dense headroom 0.10 h; subtotal 1.85 h, x1.25 reserve = 2.3 h, cap 4.0 h. Kernels: indexer scores by chunked PyTorch (fla ships only fla/ops/dsa/naive.py); sparse attention for E2 via fla Triton parallel_nsa / parallel_nsa_topk (block_indices [B,TQ,H,S], block_size 32/64; API verified in fla/ops/nsa/parallel.py); fla chunk_gdn for Qwen3.5-4B linear layers (fla README GB200 table: fwd+bwd B=2,T=16384,H=16,D=128 chunk_gdn 3.616 ms vs flash_attn 19.960 ms). Decision: xi >= 10 on at least one base and form -> gated Phase 1 (<= 8 GPU-h incl. 25% reserve: arms a-h on 0.6B at 100M tokens in one teacher stream, arms a-d replicated on qwen3.5-4b x 2 seeds, dense + L_x LoRA control 2 seeds x 60M tokens, E1 shared eval 6,000 prompts, E2 22 configurations x 1,500 prompts); xi <= 5 on both -> kill. Optional Phase 0b (hard-capped 4 GPU-h, runs either way): inference-only probe of the production QSA indexer in Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next @ de4b8e4d43b917e7706784d8bb445c9af86a3540 (180B total params, 512 experts top-10, 48 layers, QSA at 12 layers, native transformers qwen4_exp, license qwen-community-1.0 to review; ~360 GB bf16 across 8x H100), ~300 sealed prompts at 8K, gated by a 20-prompt timing probe (<= 8 s per prompt else abort). GLM-5.3-Flash (321B total params) excluded as it does not fit in bf16. Total program <= 16 GPU-h; Phase 2 (from-scratch parity-BPE hybrid, ~30 GPU-h; QSA-style CPT of qwen3.5-4b, ~170 GPU-h) is a separate contract.

candidate.kevin_advantage: The pilot depends on no private asset. What makes it easy here: 8x H100 with the Docker/Slurm/SIGUSR1-resumable harness for a shared-teacher multi-indexer job; a repository whose product is exactly the instrument this candidate delivers (per-language achieved-token ledger, selection-recall probe, sealed eval receipts); General Translation's document-level parallel pairs with in-house alignment QA as an optional upgrade for low-resource cross-script pairs (e.g. en-my/lo/am) and as the corpus for the Phase-2 CPT stage; and a genuine deployment interest (cross-lingual long-context retrieval over translation memories) that no sparse-attention lab has stated.
candidate.monitorability_and_safety: The selection set is an inspectable retrieval trace; per-language selection recall becomes an audit instrument for sparse models, including detection of cross-lingual prompt injection carried by a foreign-script block. No CoT effect. Monitored failure modes (kill condition 7): under-selection of any language, and over-selection of the other-language half in bilingual prompts (E3 monolingual regression plus a bilingual-distractor test). Data rights: ParaCrawl text CC0 with ParaDocs annotations apache-2.0; TED2020 CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (non-commercial research, no redistribution of derived text; confirm on the TED usage-policy page before the run); FineWeb-2 ODC-By 1.0; Belebele and FLORES+ CC-BY-SA 4.0; WMT24++ apache-2.0; Qwen3-0.6B-Base and Qwen3.5-4B apache-2.0; Qwen3.8-Flash-Next qwen-community-1.0 (non-standard; review before publishing probe numbers). candidate.negative_result_value: xi <= 5: the cross-lingual long-context gap in sparse models is inherited from attention mass, not from the selection component — the first component-level localization of the gap MLNeedle/OneRuler/MGAL only describe, plus a portable per-language selection-recall instrument for any DSA/QSA checkpoint. (b) ~ (c): bilingual document exposure alone repairs indexers — a free recipe for every sparse-attention lab. (d) or (e) ~ (c): a mass-concentration regularizer, not alignment content, is what indexers need. Dense+LoRA ~ (c): alignment supervision is a generic attention fix, not selection-specific, redirecting the work. Phase 0b reports whether a deployed production QSA indexer agrees with the retrofit result either way.

repairs_made: Identification 1 (circular metric: aligned-block recall equals the L_x label) -> primary endpoints are E1 needle-token selection recall defined by the needle's position and E2 generation exact match with gold answers, on sealed sources of different provenance (Belebele/WMT24++ vs ParaCrawl/TED web-and-talk training text) and on languages never seen by L_x; no evaluation quantity uses alignment labels.

Identification 2 (retrofit vs architecture; SpotAttention already publishes the frozen KL-only selector arm) -> claim_scope downgraded to attachment-capability; SpotAttention adopted as the named baseline whose non-English behaviour is the open question; production-like placement on qwen3.5-4b's 8 full-attention layers; optional inference-only probe of the production QSA indexer in Qwen3.8-Flash-Next; from-scratch/CPT arms moved to a gated Phase 2 outside the 16 GPU-h contract.

Identification 3 (token-budget confound at fixed top-k; Thai/Hindi fertility) -> k defined as a fraction of achieved haystack tokens in the model tokenizer (primary), plus fixed absolute k and needle-fertility-scaled k; SpotAttention/RTPurbo top-p mass-matched control; per-prompt achieved-token ledger (Lost in Compression protocol); haystack language equals needle language; Phase-2 parity-BPE arm.

Identification 4 (head-summed KL target may itself be the bottleneck; rank-128 not shown binding) -> the target's own top-k recall R^T is measured; the kill statistic is the excess gap xi = Delta_indexer - Delta_target; max-pooled (QSA) and retrieval-head-weighted target arms; indexer dim ladder 64/128/256.

Identification 5 (information asymmetry: L_x injects an external aligner the data control never sees) -> labels are corpus-given sentence alignments (OmniAlign/CTFAlign removed); dense + alignment-supervised LoRA control at matched tokens; L_perm negative control and L_half alternative-mechanism arm; iso-token and iso-order across arms.

Identification 6 (sparse-exceeds-dense is generic denoising already shown by QSA/FlashMemory) -> removed from the claim; kept only as exploratory P4 with oracle-selection and random-plus-needle attribution controls.

Identification 7 (aligner label noise correlated with treatment: Ja/Ko/Th AER) -> no word aligner; sentence-alignment quality is a corpus property applied uniformly across scripts; ParaDocs release filters replace the aligner threshold tau; per-pair label mass reported.

Identification 8 (WikiMatrix vs MLQA/Wikipedia contamination) -> WikiMatrix dropped; training and haystack sources are web/TED text; exact 50-gram + MinHash dedup against all eval texts with logged counts; held-out languages.

Identification 9 (dense ceiling unknown for Qwen3-0.6B) -> Phase-0 headroom gate measured first on both bases; the E1/xi kill statistic needs no generation headroom; the E2 claim is withdrawn, not rescued, if the gate fails.

Identification 10 (NMT supervised-attention prior art omitted) -> Liu 2016, Chen 2016, Garg 2019 added to what_is_new with URLs; novelty downgraded to a transfer of guided attention to a detached selection indexer with an untested diagnostic as the load-bearing claim.

votes.reason: No paper found that intervenes on the same object (a detached top-k selection indexer of a DSA/QSA-class sparse-attention LM, main attention untouched) with the same objective (a corpus-given sentence-alignment log-mass term on bilingual concatenations added to the KL distillation loss), nor any per-language selection-recall audit of a learned sparse indexer. Coverage: 13 hostsearch calls returned usable results (arXiv 3: indexer+sparse attention 25 hits, retrieval heads+cross-lingual, sparse attention+supervision/oracle; hfpapers 6; crossref 3; openreview 1 with unparsed titles), plus 10 WebSearch and 10 WebFetch/abs reads. Every indexer paper surfaced (DSA 2512.02556, QSA 2608.30320, SpotAttention 2606.22874, LongCat LSA 2608.01662, MISA 2605.07363, PIVOT 2607.24593, HISA, Full Attention Strikes Back 2605.16928, Self-Indexing KVCache, YOIO, IndexCache) trains or reuses the indexer by KL/oracle from full attention with English-centric long-context evals; none uses alignment or translation supervision and none reports per-language selection. The alignment-supervision side (Liu 2016, Chen 2016, Garg 2019 guided attention; AlignAtt4LLM 2606.03967) supervises or post-hoc selects main attention/heads, never a selection indexer; AlignAtt4LLM only selects heads offline with GPT-5-mini alignments. Lost in Compression 2608.26175 audits prompt compressors, not indexers. Routing Absorption 2603.02227 argues post-hoc frozen gating sidesteps co-adaptation, which supports rather than refutes the frozen-indexer setting. Two caveats that reduce novelty but do not refute: (1) arXiv 2606.07703 (Oracle-Guided Sparse Prefill, June 2026) already publishes a frozen-backbone, head-collapsed indexer KL-distilled from dense attention mass on Qwen3.5-0.8B/9B full/GQA layers AND an attention-mass top-k oracle that explicitly separates sparse-budget feasibility from indexer error; this is the monolingual precursor of the xi = Delta_indexer - Delta_target decomposition and of the Phase-0 baseline arm, is missing from closest_priors, and must be cited, leaving the cross-lingual axis as the only new content of P1. (2) The L_x loss itself is, as the candidate concedes, a direct transfer of NMT guided attention; the residual novelty rests on P1 being a real gap, which is untested. Coverage limits: arXiv API returned HTTP 429/empty for 10 of 13 boolean queries; DuckDuckGo blocked; OpenReview forums behind browser verification (4 hits unread); Semantic Scholar unavailable; no full-text read of QSA or GLM-5.3 reports for per-language indexer tables.

The repair fixed the aligner-imitation circularity, but the pilot as written still cannot separate the stated mechanism (a KL-only indexer fails to preserve the cross-script semantic subspace; alignment CONTENT from bilingual documents repairs it) from at least four stronger or equally matched explanations, and its decision rules never test against the strongest one.

(1) The strongest label-free control exists as an arm but is absent from every kill condition. Wave-1 objection 4 (the head-summed target itself is the bottleneck) was "repaired" by measuring R^T and adding max-pool (f) and retrieval-head-weighted (g) target arms, yet kill conditions 2-5 and P2/P3 compare (c) only against (b) = KL-head-sum-bilingual. DSA's target is literally "summing across all attention heads ... L1-normalized" (2512.02556); QSA adds max pooling precisely to preserve "salient token-level signals that could otherwise be diluted during aggregation" (2608.30320); retrieval heads are <5% of heads (2404.15574) and RTPurbo shows long-range retrieval "is governed primarily by a low-dimensional subspace, allowing relevant tokens to be retrieved efficiently with a 16-dimensional indexer" once the target is the retrieval heads rather than the head sum (2605.16928); the withdrawn RTH paper reports retrieval heads "often shared across multiple languages" (2602.22453). So a de-diluted target alone could remove most of xi with zero labels, and the pre-registered analysis would still declare P2/P3 confirmed with (c) vs (b). The QSA production recipe (max-pool) is the correct counterfactual for the block form, but (c) is KL-head-sum + L_x, so L_x's marginal value over the class it claims to fix is measured against the weaker DSA-style baseline only. Counterfactual references are inconsistent.

(2) The kill statistic xi conflates language with literal matching. In TR-NIAH the monolingual query is a verbatim copy of a needle sentence (an induction/copy task with sharp attention, Olsson et al. 2209.11895; "nearly perfect accuracy in the vanilla NIAH test", RULER 2404.06654), whereas every cross-lingual query has zero lexical overlap by construction. NoLiMa shows that removing literal overlap alone collapses retrieval even monolingually ("declines stem from the increased difficulty the attention mechanism faces ... when literal matches are absent"; GPT-4o 99.3 -> 69.7 at 32K, 2502.05167). A low-rank scorer's top-k is generically more fragile on the diffuse targets of non-literal queries, so xi >= 10 is predicted by approximation theory regardless of script. The design has no monolingual non-literal reference (paraphrase query, or Belebele question-as-query in l_N) against which to show the excess gap is cross-lingual rather than literal-vs-semantic; the same-script cross-lingual condition cannot serve because it is also non-literal.

(3) The alignment-content mechanism is unidentified against information-matched semantic supervision. L_x is a supervised set-cross-entropy that sharpens the indexer on translation pairs; E1-cross (recall of the needle = translation of the query) is the hard top-k form of the same functional on new data, so (c) > (b) is "training on task X improves X on held-out X". Because frozen LMs place "semantically equivalent inputs in different languages ... similar in the intermediate layers" (Semantic Hub 2411.04986; Wendler et al. 2402.10588), a monolingual semantic-retrieval supervision (paraphrase or QA targets, no parallel data) would plausibly transfer cross-lingually and close the same gap. No such arm exists. L_perm and L_half do not fill this role: L_half is inert for a trivial reason at eval (relative to a foreign-language query the entire haystack is "the other language"), and L_perm actively pushes mass away from the teacher's correct cross-lingual keys and so can score below (b), making "(c)-(d) >= 0.5x[(c)-(b)]" automatically satisfied; no inertness precondition (d approx b) is registered. Lost in Compression's finding that the gap "tracks compression supervision data, not architecture" (2608.26175) predicts the supervised-data win generically.

(4) E2 (the non-proxy endpoint the claim leans on) is ungated where it matters. The headroom gate is dense MONOLINGUAL E2 >= 60%; dense cross-lingual EM is never gated, though 7-8B instruct models score ~0.30 (zh), ~0.24 (ar), ~0.25 (hi) vs 0.68 English at 4K (MLNeedle 2408.10151) and instruction language alone moves results up to 20% (OneRuler 2503.01996). For a frozen 0.6B/4B base on translation-matched next-sentence copying, +8 EM for (c) over (b) is therefore either unreachable or requires (c) > dense, i.e. forced-selection renormalization, the generic denoising already shown in production (QSA > full attention, RULER 512K-1M 90.08 -> 93.00, MRCR 512K 30.66 -> 40.53, 2608.30320) that the proposal itself removed from the claim; P3 carries no (c) <= dense or oracle-sign requirement. The sparse-(b) monolingual floor is also ungated: SpotAttention's dense parity is only shown for frozen 4B-32B with dual top-p (2606.22874), and RTPurbo finds fixed top-k inferior to top-p, so 28/28 layers at fixed top-12.5% on a 0.6B model may sit at the floor where "monolingual within 2 points" is trivially true.

(5) The "information-symmetric" dense + L_x LoRA control is neither symmetric nor matched: its gain is dense-vs-dense while (c)-(b) is sparse-vs-sparse at k=12.5% (different headroom), and it conflates bilingual LM fine-tuning with L_x (no LM-loss-only LoRA arm), so kill condition 5 is nearly untriggerable and biases toward "selection-specific".

(6) P1's population is wrong for a class claim: held-out languages are absent from the indexer's KL training (bilingual pairs are en-{de,fr,es,pl,th,hi,km,zh,ru,ar}; monolingual filler "in the same languages"), so xi on ja/ko/bn/ta/el/he/ka measures OOD transfer of a 50M-token frozen retrofit (DSA's frozen warm-up alone is 2.1B tokens, then 943.7B unfrozen), not a property of "DSA/QSA-class" indexers trained on ~1T multilingual tokens; the in-training cross-script pairs that would be the right P1 population are secondary, and the class-level claim sentence still reads a retrofit result as a class property despite the scope label.

Minor: the proposal's "RTPurbo 2608.26449" resolves to an unrelated abugida-tokenizer paper (RTPurbo is 2605.16928); no needle-absent control guards E2 against parametric recall of FLORES/Belebele passages; "larger k at matched latency" is undefined for (c) vs (b), which share identical cost. Salvage would require: pre-registering (c) vs (f)/(g) and (f)+L_x vs (f) as the primary counterfactual; a monolingual non-literal reference for xi; an information-matched monolingual semantic-supervision arm; a dense cross-lingual and sparse-(b) monolingual headroom gate with an oracle-sign requirement on P3; inertness preconditions on L_perm/L_half; an LM-loss-only LoRA arm; and xi reported primarily on in-training cross-script pairs.

disc.delta_one_sentence: Text A's indexer (sum_j w_{t,j} ReLU(q^I_{t,j}.k^I_s)), top-k 2048 selection, and frozen-backbone KL distillation from the head-summed dense attention are DSA's lightning indexer and dense-warm-up stage reproduced verbatim, so the only mechanistic delta is the added auxiliary loss L_x that pushes indexer mass onto the parallel-corpus-aligned sentence in the other language (plus QSA block-form, max-pool and retrieval-head-weighted aggregation arms and the L_perm/L_half controls) — a supervised cross-lingual alignment signal DSA's indexer never receives, since DSA trains it purely by self-distillation from the main model's attention with no parallel data, alignment labels, or block-level selection, and DSA's own extra piece (the sparse stage that unfreezes the backbone) is deliberately dropped by Text A, so neither strictly subsumes the other.

judges.fatal_defect: Identification (refuter confidence 0.72, and I concur): the pre-registered counterfactual for every L_x claim is arm (b) = KL-to-head-sum, the weakest target aggregation in the class the candidate says it fixes. The de-diluted target arms (f) max-pool/QSA-recipe and (g) retrieval-head-weighted are listed as controls but appear in no prediction (P2/P3) and no kill condition, so a label-free target fix that removes most of xi would leave P2/P3 'confirmed' and the alignment-content mechanism unidentified. Compounding this, the kill statistic xi compares a verbatim-copy monolingual query (induction-sharp attention) against a zero-lexical-overlap cross-lingual query with no monolingual non-literal reference row, so xi >= 10 is predicted by literal-vs-semantic retrieval fragility alone (NoLiMa-style) regardless of script. Secondary defects that do not reject but cost points: no information-matched monolingual semantic-supervision arm (paraphrase/QA targets, no parallel data) to separate 'alignment content' from 'any semantic sharpening'; dense cross-lingual E2 headroom and the sparse-(b) monolingual floor are ungated while P3 demands +8 EM with no oracle-sign or (c) <= dense requirement; L_perm has no inertness precondition so '(c)-(d) >= half of (c)-(b)' is near-automatic; the dense+LoRA control conflates bilingual LM fine-tuning with L_x and compares dense-vs-dense against sparse-vs-sparse; no power/CI/paired-SE specification behind the 3-seed thresholds; and Oracle-Guided Sparse Prefill (arXiv 2606.07703, frozen-backbone KL indexer plus attention-mass top-k oracle on Qwen3.5-0.8B/9B) is the monolingual precursor of the xi decomposition and is absent from closest_priors, with 10 of 13 arXiv queries returning 429 and 4 OpenReview hits unread (cap 74 applies on coverage; cap 79 applies because no model loop, benchmark adapter, container smoke run or Slurm dry-run is attested; cap 89 applies for no provider-distinct review). Feasibility is sound (independently re-derived 1.88 GPU-h base vs 4.0 cap), with fixable caveats: fla parallel_nsa asserts HQ/H >= 16 which both bases fail, Phase 0b's 8 s x 300 abort threshold (5.3 GPU-h) exceeds its own 4 GPU-h cap, Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B is the post-trained checkpoint, and Phase 0 lacks an indexer-adequacy gate so an under-trained indexer can yield a false kill.
judges.highest_impact_fix: Re-register the identification so L_x must beat the strongest label-free repair and xi isolates language from literalness: (1) make the primary counterfactual (f)+L_x vs (f) and (g)+L_x vs (g) (QSA max-pool and retrieval-head-weighted targets), and change kill condition 2 to 'L_x recovers < 30% of the residual xi after the best label-free target aggregation'; report (c) vs (b) only as the DSA-style secondary. (2) Add a monolingual non-literal reference row to the E1 ledger (Belebele question-as-query or a paraphrased needle in the needle language) and redefine xi as cross-lingual gap minus monolingual-non-literal gap, each measured against the target's own R^T. (3) Add an information-matched monolingual semantic-supervision arm (same set-cross-entropy loss form on paraphrase/QA targets, no parallel data, iso-token) and require L_x to beat it on held-out cross-script pairs by at least half of its own recovery. (4) Register inertness preconditions (|d - b| <= 1 point, |e - b| <= 1 point) before the L_perm/L_half comparisons count, add an LM-loss-only LoRA arm, gate P3 on dense cross-lingual E2 >= 40% and sparse-(b) monolingual E1 >= R^T - 5, and require (c) <= dense or oracle-sign agreement for any E2 gain. (5) Cite arXiv 2606.07703 in closest_priors as the monolingual precursor of the xi decomposition, fix the RTPurbo id to 2605.16928, add a Phase-0 indexer-adequacy gate (English monolingual indexer recall within 5 points of R^T), pad Q heads or use a gather path for fla parallel_nsa, lower the Phase 0b abort threshold to 6 s, and switch the 4B base to Qwen3.5-4B-Base or relabel it as post-trained. Before Phase 1, attest a model-loop smoke run, non-stub NIAH adapter, container smoke run and Slurm dry-run to lift the 79 cap.

judges.fatal_defect: The load-bearing kill statistic xi = Delta_ind - Delta_T is not identified as a cross-lingual quantity: the monolingual reference query is a verbatim copy of the needle sentence (a literal-match/induction task with sharp attention), while every cross-lingual query has zero lexical overlap by construction, so a low-rank top-k scorer is expected to show an excess gap of >= 10 points on the diffuse non-literal target regardless of script (NoLiMa-style collapse) and P1 would 'confirm' a cross-lingual bottleneck that is really a literal-vs-semantic one. The same chain then measures L_x only against the weakest baseline: P2/P3 and kill conditions 2-5 compare (c) = head-sum-KL + L_x with (b) = head-sum-KL, although the label-free de-diluted targets (f) max-pool/QSA and (g) retrieval-head-weighted are already in the arm list and could remove most of xi with zero labels, so the pre-registered analysis can declare the mechanism confirmed while alignment content contributes nothing. Secondary but cap-relevant: closest_priors omits arXiv 2606.07703 (Oracle-Guided Sparse Prefill), the monolingual precursor of the indexer-vs-attention-mass-oracle decomposition and of the Phase-0 baseline arm, so novelty coverage is incomplete (cap 74); the pilot is designed but not executable (NIAH/TR-NIAH builder and selection-recall instrument are declared deliverables, no container smoke run or Slurm dry-run attested, and fla parallel_nsa asserts HQ/H >= 16 which both pinned bases fail, so the E2 kernel path as written does not run); and no provider-distinct signed review exists yet (cap 89).
judges.highest_impact_fix: Redefine the Phase-0 kill statistic so both legs are non-literal and the counterfactual is the strongest label-free arm: (1) add a monolingual paraphrase/question-as-query reference in the needle language (Belebele question or a held-out paraphrase of the needle, same prompts, same k) and define Delta_ind and Delta_T as cross-lingual-non-literal minus monolingual-non-literal recall, reporting the literal-copy condition only as a ceiling; (2) pre-register (f) max-pool and (g) retrieval-head-weighted KL-only indexers as the baseline for every L_x claim, with the primary P2/P3 contrast being (f)+L_x versus (f) (and (g)+L_x versus (g)) and kill condition 2 rewritten as 'a de-diluted label-free target recovers >= 80% of xi'; (3) add an inertness precondition (d approx b within 1 point) before L_perm can serve as a negative control, and a dense cross-lingual E2 headroom gate plus oracle-sign requirement on P3. Alongside, cite 2606.07703 in closest_priors with its delta, and attest a CPU-only executable pilot (TR-NIAH builder doctor, achieved-token ledger, a 20-prompt indexer-vs-target recall smoke run in the pinned container with a Slurm dry-run, and a head-padding or gather path for parallel_nsa) before the first GPU job is submitted.

candidate.claim: A fixed-size recurrent state that stores meaning should write the same segment delta for two translations of a span. On a matched hybrid/dense pair (Olmo-Hybrid-7B vs Olmo-3-1025-7B), translation-paired MQAR with state-level interventions (delta-zeroing, training-free delta transport, delta swap) first measures whether a 2026 GDN hybrid's recurrent state stores meaning or surface (phase 0 kill screen). If the state carries recall, shows a hybrid-specific cross-lingual gap, and a training-free linear transport cannot close it, then supervising the per-head state delta on public bitext in half the GDN heads closes >= 50% of that gap at equal monolingual recall and LM loss and beats a same-layer projection-alignment control that has no recurrence (phase 1).
candidate.mechanism: GDN layers S_t = S_{t-1}(alpha_t(I - beta_t k_t k_t^T)) + beta_t v_t k_t^T (fla chunk_gated_delta_rule; initial_state in, final state out, backward accepts dht). For a parallel span pair (a^A, a^B) after a shared prefix c, the per-head segment delta D^{(l,h)}(a|c) = S(c+a) - S(c), with S_before bitwise identical across the pair. Treatment (A1): L = L_LM + lambda(L_eq + L_nce) on head subset E (half the heads per GDN layer); L_eq = mean_{l,h in E}(1 - cos(vec D^A, vec D^B)); L_nce = InfoNCE over in-batch deltas (tau 0.07) with >= 2 hard negatives per anchor that share a named entity or number with a^A but are not its translation; lambda in {0.1, 0.3}. Decisive control (A2): identical loss on P(a) = sum_t beta_t v_t k_t^T, the decay-free erase-free bilinear pooling of the same E heads' projections over the same span (same layers, heads, shape, lambda, tau, negatives) so A1 - A2 isolates the recurrence-aware write. Placebo (A3): identical loss with a^B replaced by a content-independent random span of language B (language-marginal pairing, provably carries no information about a^A's content). Instrument TP-MQAR-v2: N facts '<key sentence in A> <sep_A> <4-digit ASCII code>' among distractors in A, query '<translated key in B> <sep_B>', exact match on digits only; key x query language matrix; N in {8, 32}; keys split into surface-disjoint (no shared alphanumeric token >= 3 chars or digit string after NFKC/casefold; primary endpoint) and surface-shared (copy-shortcut probe). State-level interventions without gradients: D-zero (S <- S_before after the fact span), training-free per-head ridge transport W_h fitted on FLORES+ dev deltas (S <- S_before + unvec(W_h vec D^A)), and swap (S <- S_before + D^B). Phase-1 hybrids use sliding-window-512 attention in the 1-in-4 attention layers so beyond-window recall is state-carried by construction; the dense control is a full-attention transformer.
candidate.what_is_new: Downgraded per the novelty refuter: the loss form (translation-pair cosine + InfoNCE) is standard, and MQAR, cross-lingual NIAH (MLNeedle, OneRuler) and the functional-swap criterion (GI-SAE) exist. What has no located prior is (a) the object — the per-head recurrent-state segment delta of a GDN hybrid — as the target of a translation-equivariance loss, and (b) the instrument — translation-paired recall with state-level interventions (delta-zeroing, training-free delta transport, delta swap) on a matched hybrid/dense pair. The Olmo pair has been used once as a matched instrument (2606.20936: monolingual token-level loss, no cross-lingual axis, no state intervention). No direct prior art found through 2026-09-01 under arXiv API x7, HF papers x2, OpenReview x1 (forums CAPTCHA-blocked) plus the wave-1 novelty refuter's ~21 queries.

closest_priors.title: Olmo Hybrid: From Theory to Practice and Back
closest_priors.delta: The substrate: 7B 3:1 GDN hybrid trained on the Olmo 3 data mix (6T tokens, throughput-matched per Ai2 blog); no cross-lingual or state-level recall analysis.

falsifiable_predictions: P0a (phase 0, frozen, surface-disjoint keys, N=16, 4K, En<->De and En<->Es): Olmo-Hybrid-7B's cross-lingual gap G = EM[A=B] - EM[A!=B] exceeds Olmo-3-1025-7B's by >= 8 EM points (paired bootstrap 95% CI excluding 0); embarrassing if the gaps are within 3 points.
P0b (D-zero): zeroing the fact's GDN span deltas in all 24 linear layers of Olmo-Hybrid-7B removes >= 30% of its cross-lingual recall (relative); embarrassing if <= 10% (attention carries recall).

P0c (training-free transport): per-head ridge transport fitted on FLORES+ dev closes <= 40% of the hybrid's gap on devtest keys; embarrassing if >= 80% (state already stores meaning up to a linear transform).

P1 (phase 1, 57M SWA-512+GDN hybrids, 3 seeds, beyond-window facts, surface-disjoint keys): A1 closes >= 50% of A0's cross-lingual gap with monolingual EM within 2 points and held-out LM loss within 0.5%; A2 (projection control) closes <= 25%; A3 (placebo) <= 10%; A1 - A2 >= 5 points and same-signed in all 3 seed pairs.

P2 (shortcut and swap): A1's closure on surface-disjoint keys is within 10 points of its closure on surface-shared keys; swapping D^A -> D^B in E heads preserves >= 80% of recall in A1 vs <= 40% in A0.
kill_conditions: Phase 0: hybrid-specific gap <= 3 points (states already store meaning; publish the instrument result, stop the training arm); or D-zero removes <= 10% of recall (state is not the carrier); or training-free transport closes >= 80% of the gap (training redundant).

Phase 1: A1 does not beat A2 by >= 5 points paired over seeds (projection alignment suffices); or A3 closes >= 50% of what A1 closes (regularization, not equivariance); or closure appears on surface-shared keys but not surface-disjoint keys (copy shortcut).
Collapse or tax: held-out LM loss > 1% worse, or mean ||D|| in E heads shrinks > 30%; or A5 (no bitext) equals A0 within 2 points while A1 is only better than A5 (effect is bitext exposure).

Abort gates (not reinterpretation): monolingual A=B EM at N=8 must be >= 60% in both Olmo models for a language, else the language is dropped; if no non-English language passes, phase 0 cannot run on this pair and only instrument-only cells with no causal claim remain. Phase-1 A0 monolingual in-window EM must reach >= 70% at N=8 at 200M tokens, else phase 1 is extended under a new budget line.
candidate.cheapest_decisive_pilot: Phase 0 kill screen (<= 3.2 GPU-h on the 8xH100 node, 2 GPUs in parallel). The wave-2 repairs fixed the surface-shortcut, value-translation and bitext-null issues, but the pilot as written still cannot separate its mechanism ("the GDN state stores surface, and supervising the recurrent write fixes it") from confounds and from its own strongest control. Six concrete failures:

(1) The phase-0 "matched pair" premise is false on Ai2's own sources, so the difference-of-differences (P0a, kill 1) is unidentified. The candidate asserts "same 6T Olmo 3 data mix ... at 4K the only architectural difference is 24 GDN vs 24 softmax layers". The Olmo-Hybrid-7B model card says the opposite: "we change the learning rate schedule to be a standard cosine schedule rather than the piecewise schedule used by Olmo 3. Additionally, we use the improved data mix of Olmo 3 32B instead of the Olmo 3 7B mix"; stage-1 tokens 5.50T (hybrid, dataset allenai/dolma3_mix-6T) vs 5.93T (Olmo 3 7B, dolma3_mix-6T-1025); hidden 3840 vs 4096; 30 vs 32 heads; GDN head dims 96/192 (doubled); hybrid stage-2 = "2 versions ... merged" vs Olmo 3 7B "No merging". The Ai2 blog says "Training throughput was matched", not data — and reports the hybrid reaches Olmo 3's MMLU with 49% fewer tokens and RULER-64K 85.0 vs 70.9, i.e. a generally stronger model. Worse for a recall probe: the released hybrid checkpoint has rope_parameters.rope_theta = null and transformers' modeling_olmo_hybrid.py states "Released ckpt don't use any ROPE" (NoPE attention), whereas Olmo-3-1025-7B uses RoPE theta 5e5 with YaRN. So the 8 shared full-attention layers — the layers Gather-and-Aggregate (2504.18574) and Attention Amnesia (2606.11052) identify as the recall carriers in hybrids — differ in positional encoding. A >= 8-point extra cross-lingual gap in the hybrid is attributable to NoPE-vs-RoPE attention, data mix, schedule, width or merging as readily as to GDN storage; the language-competence gate (monolingual EM >= 60%) does not equalize En<->De/Es translation-equivalence competence, which is what the cross-lingual cell needs and which the two different mixes need not share.

(2) Even with a truly matched pair, "state stores surface" is not identified against readout interference. GDN reads with an unnormalized linear readout q^T S; a translated query whose similarity margin over N-1 distractors is reduced (by the same amount in both architectures, since the residual-stream representations come from the same data) yields interference growing with N in the hybrid but is rescued by softmax's winner-take-all in the dense model. Under this account the state stores exactly the same content as attention's K cache, and P0a, P0b (state necessary), P0c (transport fails, see 4) and even a positive P1 (an equivariance loss raises the margin) all come out identical. Recurrent-recall interference is the documented failure mode of fixed-size states (Zoology 2312.04927; Based 2402.18668), and 2606.20936 shows on this very pair that the hybrid's loss advantage "nearly vanishes on repeated n-grams", i.e. monolingual copy competence already differs, so bounded-EM gap differences also carry floor/ceiling compression. No N-scaling or margin contrast is registered to separate storage format from readout.

(3) The training objective leaks the shared prefix, so A1 - A2 does not isolate a "recurrence-aware write", and the P2 swap endpoint is the training objective. With per-head scalar decay (fla chunk_gated_delta_rule takes g of shape [B,T,H]), D(a|c) = (prod_t alpha_t) S(c) prod_t(I - beta_t k_t k_t^T) - S(c) + writes; if E-head write strengths shrink, the erase term tends to (prod alpha - 1) S(c), which is identical for a^A and a^B irrespective of content. The candidate's negatives are "the batch's other spans PLUS >= 2 hard negatives ... entity-grouped sampling from the bitext" — all behind their own prefixes; the positive is the only in-batch pair sharing S(c) (bitwise identical by construction). Both L_eq and L_nce are therefore minimizable through prefix identity and the decay gate alpha (a forgetting/capacity change) with zero translation equivariance; the "mean ||D|| shrinks > 30%" kill does not fire because the prefix term inflates ||D||. A2's pooling P(a) = sum beta_t v_t k_t^T has no S(c) term, so A1 - A2 >= 5 points is exactly what the shortcut produces. The swap criterion (S <- S_before + D^B preserves >= 80% recall in A1) is a monotone function of cos(D^A, D^B), the quantity A1 minimizes directly. Fix needed: same-prefix negatives and a delta defined net of (prod alpha) S(c).

(4) The training-free transport gate (P0c, kill 3) cannot fire. Per-head ridge W_h on vec D in R^{96x192 = 18,432} has 3.4e8 parameters per head (720 heads), fitted on 2 x 997 FLORES+ dev pairs; with rank capped by SVD the fitted map has rank <= ~2,000 in an 18,432-dim space and is heavily shrunk, so "<= 40% closure" is guaranteed by estimation error, not by state semantics. Passing this gate is not evidence about the state.

(5) The placebo A3 is not inert and its prefix structure is unspecified. Language-marginal pairing with cosine + InfoNCE pushes every language-A delta toward language-B deltas regardless of content — a language-ID-removal (domain-confusion) objective on the state, itself a plausible mechanism for closing a cross-lingual gap. A3 ~ A1 would not mean "regularization", and A1 > A3 would not exclude that A1 acts through language-ID removal. Likewise D-zero (P0b) has no matched-perturbation control (D-zero on an equal-length distractor span); zeroing all 24 layers' deltas while attention KV keeps the span is an out-of-distribution state/KV inconsistency, so recall lost is an upper bound on "state's share".

(6) claim_scope "architecture-causal" is a misread: the only causal contrast (A1 vs A0/A2/A3) is an auxiliary loss on a fixed 57M SWA-512 architecture; A4 (full attention, recall attention-carried by construction) is descriptive, and phase 1's "state-carried by construction" regime is not the regime phase 0 measures (7B, full attention every 4th layer, NoPE), so phase-0 kills do not license phase-1 inferences. Also the surface-disjoint filter is word-level (NFKC/casefold tokens >= 3 chars) while the copy shortcut for En<->De/Es operates at the BPE level (cognates share subwords).
